question.prompt: Una rolls \(6\) standard \(6\)-sided dice simultaneously and calculates the product of the \(6\) numbers obtained. What is the probability that the product is divisible by \(4?\)

solutions.title: Count the failures
solutions.explanation:
Divisibility by \(4\) requires at least two factors of \(2\), so the failures have very few possible forms. An odd roll contributes no factors of \(2\), a roll of \(2\) or \(6\) contributes one, and a roll of \(4\) already contributes two.

Thus the product fails to be divisible by \(4\) in exactly two disjoint cases:

1. Every die is odd. Each die has three odd faces, so independence gives probability
\[
\left(\frac36\right)^6=\frac1{64}.
\]
2. Exactly one die shows \(2\) or \(6\), and the other five are odd. There are six choices for that one die. For each choice, the probability is \(\frac26(\frac36)^5\). These choices cannot overlap, because each outcome has a unique even die. Their total probability is
\[
6\cdot\frac26\cdot\left(\frac36\right)^5=\frac1{16}.
\]

These cases cover every product with fewer than two factors of \(2\). Subtracting their total probability from \(1\), we obtain
\[
1-\frac1{64}-\frac1{16}=\boxed{\frac{59}{64}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
